note: Authored 2026-08-10 by the T-0022 lane from six swarm research reports carrying 232 sources. These are the sources the pack body, guides, refs and checks actually cite; the rest stay in the reports and in research/NOTES.md. The pack cites FRAG ids because assigning EV ids is the integrator's step: run tools/import_fragments.py, then rewrite every FRAG-AGENTIC-SWARM-NN citation outside this directory to the id the import assigned, or check S014 fails on every pack file. Six records deduplicate by URL into rows that already exist and so keep those ids rather than gaining new ones: 05 into EV-0109, 12 into EV-0112, 13 into EV-0053, 14 into EV-0108, 25 into EV-0244, 50 into EV-0013. None of those six is cited by FRAG id anywhere in the read surface, because the pack already cites the existing EV ids for them. Every other record is cited exactly once or more, so no row should import uncited.

records.source: When Parallelism Pays Off: Cohesion-Aware Task Partitioning for Multi-Agent Coding (Co-Coder)
records.study_design: system paper with baseline comparison against sequential, file-per-agent and vendor agent-team configurations
records.population: 28 tasks across two Python repository benchmarks
records.model: not stated per arm in the material read
records.licence: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence; code repository licence not stated
records.finding: Cutting the partition on dependency-graph cohesion, with structural hub files isolated at an in-degree ratio above 0.4, beat sequential work on pass rate (68.1 against 56.8 on DevEval, 34.1 against 20.1 on CodeProjectEval) at 0.65 to 0.72 times the cost. Cutting one file per agent cost 1.44 to 1.60 times sequential for 0.9 and 3.2 points. An unpartitioned vendor agent team was cheaper and faster than sequential and scored below it on both benchmarks.
records.applicability_limits: Python repositories only, 28 tasks, no ablation over partition count or over the 0.4 threshold; the dependency blueprint is model-generated so its errors propagate; near-complete coupling degrades the method to sequential; the agent-team baseline is a third party's configuration of another vendor's tool.
records.counter_evidence: The same table shows the unstructured agent team at 0.25 to 0.67 times wall-clock and 0.37 to 0.92 times cost. A team optimising cycle time rather than correctness reads this result the opposite way.

records.source: Do More Agents Help? Controlled and Protocol-Aligned Evaluation of LLM Agent Workflows (BenchAgent)
records.study_design: normalised substrate holding benchmark loading, tool access, accounting and logging constant across single-agent, fixed multi-agent and self-evolving multi-agent systems
records.population: ten benchmarks, six multi-agent systems against one single-agent baseline
records.model: GPT-4.1 for the controlled arm; Claude Code for the protocol-aligned external study
records.finding: Under one normalised substrate the single-agent baseline scored 74.12 per cent at 27,435 average tokens. The best multi-agent system reached 75.56 per cent, inside the uncertainty band, at 24 per cent more tokens; the other five scored 62.83 to 71.56 per cent, one of them at 286 per cent more tokens. Separately, a runtime-generated workflow scored 66.72 per cent on GAIA against 46.66 per cent for the strongest other baseline, and 69.23 against 19.23 per cent at Level 3, at lower token cost.
records.applicability_limits: Authors call the comparison controlled but not fully causal; the multi-agent reimplementations may not reproduce the original designs; single-run pass@1 with no repeated trials; the runtime-generated-workflow advantage confounds workflow generation, compaction, tooling, permission scoping and provider bookkeeping.
records.counter_evidence: The GAIA result cuts against a blanket anti-swarm reading: what lost was fixed hand-authored topology, not fan-out over task structure.

records.source: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
records.study_design: 260 controlled configurations over six benchmarks, five agent-system architectures and three model families, with architecture selection tested on held-out configurations
records.population: six benchmark task sets spanning decomposable finance, web research, sequential planning and tool-heavy work
records.model: three model families under five agent-system architectures
records.benchmark: six benchmarks reported in arXiv v3
records.finding: Agent topology is task-shaped. Version 3 reports an 80.8 per cent gain on a decomposable finance task and a 70 per cent loss on sequential planning, with coordination overhead on tool-heavy work, error propagation without central verification and 87 per cent held-out architecture selection. Its data-derived capability-saturation check reports negative returns above roughly 45 per cent single-agent success and a 94 per cent match across the reported 16-model, two-benchmark check.
records.applicability_limits: These are benchmark results rather than a repository-software study. Outcomes depend on the tested model families, harness, task graph, tool load, budget and oracle. The 45 per cent result is a study threshold to test locally, not a universal EOS cut-off. The paper is a preprint and its fitted model leaves most variance unexplained.
records.counter_evidence: The 80.8 per cent improvement is strong evidence that a coordinated multi-agent topology can help a decomposable task. The sequential and tool-heavy losses show why that result cannot become a general swarm default.

records.source: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
records.study_design: budget-matched comparison holding reasoning tokens constant rather than holding architecture constant
records.population: multi-hop reasoning benchmark sets across three model families
records.model: Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama, Gemini 2.5
records.finding: With reasoning tokens held equal, single-agent systems consistently match or beat multi-agent systems on multi-hop reasoning. The information-theoretic account is that a single agent is strictly more efficient under a fixed budget unless its context utilisation degrades or the multi-agent system is quietly given more compute.
records.applicability_limits: Multi-hop reasoning, not software construction. Authors flag artefacts in API-side budget control and in benchmarks that can inflate multi-agent numbers.
records.counter_evidence: The stated exception is the precondition that makes fan-out legitimate: fan-out earns its keep exactly when one context would degrade, and context-rot measurement shows that degradation is real.

records.source: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST taxonomy)
records.study_design: failure-mode taxonomy from expert annotation of execution traces with an inter-annotator agreement study
records.population: 1,600+ annotated traces across seven multi-agent frameworks, taxonomy derived from 150 expert-annotated traces
records.model: GPT-4, Claude 3, Qwen2.5, CodeLlama era
records.benchmark: coding, maths and general agent tasks
records.finding: Multi-agent failures fall into three categories at inter-annotator kappa 0.88: specification and system design, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification. The largest share sits in specification and design, and the smallest in verification, so most multi-agent failure originates before or between the lanes rather than in the checking step. The authors' own framing is that multi-agent gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal.
records.applicability_limits: Traces come from 2024 and 2025 framework generations, so absolute rates have moved; the taxonomy is diagnostic and proves no topology better than another; CC BY-NC-ND forbids adapting the taxonomy text verbatim; the authors report that their own interventions yield limited results. The widely quoted numeric split between the three categories differs between secondary reports and could not be confirmed against the primary PDF, so the ordering of the categories is used here and the percentages are not.
records.counter_evidence: Verification being the smallest of the three categories argues against over-investing in review relative to specification and handoff design.

records.source: AI Agent Pull Requests on GitHub: Frequency, Structure, and Merge Conflict Rates
records.study_design: observational mining of agent-authored pull requests with textual merge-conflict detection over temporally co-active pairs
records.population: 33,596 pull requests across 2,807 repositories, December 2024 to July 2025
records.model: Codex, Copilot, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code
records.finding: Concurrent agent pull requests from the same agent conflicted textually at 19.8 per cent per pair (95 per cent CI 16.8 to 23.2); cross-agent pairs conflicted at 41.7 per cent (CI 33.1 to 50.9), with non-overlapping intervals. Conflicted files were 84.4 per cent source code, and 42 per cent of conflicts were structural (modify-delete plus add-add), which three-way merge handles worst.
records.applicability_limits: Textual detection only, described by the authors as a conservative lower bound with no build or semantic conflicts measured; temporal co-activity is a proxy for concurrent work; cross-agent sample is 115 pairs; open source only; the authors caution that the low cross-agent rate may partly reflect per-agent mining.
records.counter_evidence: One agent in the sample showed 39.7 per cent co-activity against 80 per cent or more for the others, so a single-vendor fleet sits at a different point on the exposure curve than the dataset average.

records.source: BulkPR-Bench: Benchmarking Queue-Level Governance of Interacting Pull Requests
records.study_design: constructed benchmark under progressive information revelation with a tunable batch size
records.population: 581 constructed candidates over 18 repository snapshots, six models, three runs per cell
records.model: six coding models including Claude-Opus-4.8 and Kimi-K3
records.finding: Agents recalled the critical relations between queued changes only 35.2 to 57.7 per cent of the time, but respected relations they had identified 98.1 to 100 per cent of the time; handing them the true relations raised the delivery score by 22.3 to 50.2 points. Left to infer, 69.8 per cent of runs committed unsafe merges and only 8.3 per cent produced a deployable non-empty plan.
records.applicability_limits: One designed candidate pool per snapshot; the authors state results do not generalise to natural queue frequencies or other projects; one scaffold, prompt and turn budget for all models; three runs per cell incompletely characterise variation; it measures repository reasoning, not production correctness.
records.counter_evidence: Batching was not monotonic: most models improved from batch size 1 to 32 but one peaked at 8 and then declined, so batch size is tunable rather than bigger-is-better.

records.source: Mergify, State of Merge Queues 2026
records.study_design: telemetry analysis over a rolling 90-day window with repository-level filtering
records.population: 200,000+ merges across 477 organisations; filtered analysis 153,000 merges across about 160 organisations
records.licence: Data licensed CC BY 4.0 as stated in the report
records.finding: Broken-main rate rises with the writing population: 0.77 per cent at two to five developers, 0.98 per cent at six to fifteen, 2.49 per cent at sixteen to forty and 12.5 per cent above forty. Only 6 per cent of private merges batch, average batch four, and automation merges roughly fifteen times faster than manual.
records.applicability_limits: Only tools leaving commit signatures are detectable, so the AI share is a floor; autonomous agent pull requests were a few hundred of 153,000, so this is human-driven merging with assistance rather than swarm data.
records.counter_evidence: AI-assisted pull requests broke main less often than unassisted ones, 1.9 against 4.4 per cent, holding across sizes and within the same repositories, which is genuine counter-evidence to the assumption that agent code destabilises trunk.

records.source: LinearB, 8 million pull requests reveal where engineering productivity breaks down
records.study_design: vendor telemetry across customer organisations, classification method not disclosed
records.population: 8.1 million pull requests, 4,800 teams, 42 countries, early 2024 to May 2026
records.finding: AI-generated pull requests merged within 30 days at 32.7 per cent against 84.5 per cent for unassisted ones, waited roughly five times longer to be picked up, and were about 2.6 times larger. The refactor rate in AI-assisted pull requests was near zero against about 37 per cent unassisted.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor telemetry from one product's customers, not a random sample; no licence stated; the AI-assisted, AI-generated and agentic labels are the vendor's and the detection method is undisclosed; secondary reporting gives slightly different pickup multiples.
records.counter_evidence: Once picked up, AI-generated pull requests had a shorter review cycle than unassisted ones, so the delay is queueing rather than comprehension. That points at reviewer capacity, not at unreadable code.

records.source: Faros AI, AI Code Quality: The Hidden Cost Senior Engineers Pay
records.study_design: correlational comparison of high-adoption against low-adoption teams in vendor telemetry
records.population: 22,000 developers across 4,000 teams over two years
records.finding: Under high AI adoption against low, pull request size rose 51.3 per cent, files per pull request 59.7 per cent, bugs per pull request 54 per cent, median time in review 441.5 per cent, and pull requests merged with no review at all 31.3 per cent.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor telemetry, no licence, no disclosed definition of high adoption and no method for constructing the comparison groups; correlational, so high-adoption teams may differ systematically.
records.counter_evidence: It cuts against the merge-queue telemetry showing AI-assisted changes breaking main less often. Both cannot be straightforwardly true of the same population and neither source establishes the reconciliation.

records.source: SlopCodeBench: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Degrade Over Long-Horizon Iterative Tasks
records.study_design: checkpointed long-horizon extension benchmark calibrated against maintained human repositories
records.population: 20 problems, 93 checkpoints, calibrated against 48 maintained Python repositories
records.model: frontier coding models including Claude Opus 4.6
records.finding: Structural erosion rose in 80 per cent of agent trajectories and verbosity in 89.8 per cent. Mean high-complexity function counts went from 4.1 to 37.0 while human repositories stayed stable. The authors conclude that pass-rate benchmarks systematically undermeasure extension robustness.
records.applicability_limits: Python only; 20 problems; and critically it measures degradation over sequential iterations, not over parallel lane count, so it is not lane-count evidence.
records.counter_evidence: None on its own terms. Its scope is regularly misquoted as evidence about parallel agents and it is not.

records.source: How we built our multi-agent research system (Anthropic)
records.model: Claude Opus 4 lead with Claude Sonnet 4 subagents
records.finding: Agents use about four times the tokens of a chat and multi-agent systems about fifteen times. Token usage alone explained about 80 per cent of performance variance on one benchmark. The brief contract is four fields: objective, output format, guidance on tools and sources, and clear task boundaries; a vague brief produced duplicate searches and misinterpretation. The vendor states the pattern is a poor fit for domains needing shared context or heavy interdependency, such as most coding tasks.
records.applicability_limits: Internal evaluation on open-ended search, not code change; methodology not published; the headline uplift is reported rather than independently reproducible.
records.counter_evidence: The vendor's own caution against generalising its result to coding is the direct counter to using this post as support for a coding swarm.

records.source: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes (Anthropic)
records.study_design: single uncontrolled case study
records.population: one greenfield compiler project, about 2,000 sessions over nearly two weeks
records.model: Claude, 16 parallel agents in containers
records.benchmark: C conformance suites, differential comparison against GCC
records.licence: not-stated for reuse; page carries an Anthropic copyright notice
records.finding: Sixteen lanes produced a 100,000-line compiler for about 20,000 dollars, coordinating through claim files in git rather than a message bus, with no dedicated integration agent. The author states that the task verifier must be nearly perfect or the model solves the wrong problem. Compiling one monolithic target made all sixteen agents hit identical bugs at once and parallelism was useless until the failure surface was split with delta debugging.
records.applicability_limits: One case, no control, no comparison against fewer agents, no stated optimum. The domain is maximally favourable: a written specification, public conformance suites, a reference implementation to diff against and per-test decidable correctness, on greenfield code with no legacy coupling.
records.counter_evidence: The same post is the strongest argument for wide fan-out and the strongest argument against weakening verification. It also lists real defects, including frequent feature additions breaking existing functionality near the end.

records.source: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions (agent teams documentation)
records.finding: The lead's conversation history does not carry over, so the spawn prompt is the only channel. Two teammates editing one file leads to overwrites, so the work must be partitioned by file ownership. Messages between agents are untrusted: a teammate cannot approve a permission prompt on the user's behalf and a denied teammate cannot relay through another to bypass the check. Teammates start with the lead's permission settings, including a permission-skipping flag, and per-teammate modes cannot be set at spawn.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor guidance with no published supporting data behind its sizing figures; the feature is experimental and off by default; behaviour is version-specific and moved repeatedly inside two months.
records.counter_evidence: An independent benchmark measured this configuration scoring below a sequential baseline on pass rate, so following the documentation without an explicit partition is not sufficient.

records.source: Run parallel sessions with worktrees (Claude Code documentation)
records.finding: Worktree isolation is enforced by the harness through three checks: edits targeting the main checkout are blocked, commands whose working directory resolves to the main checkout or cannot be verified as outside it are blocked, and git redirects into the main checkout are blocked whether by flag, environment variable or a directory change. A manifest file carries ignored configuration such as environment files into each new worktree so a lane can verify itself.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation, version-specific, with no data on how many parallel worktrees are safe. Worktrees share the git directory, which is what enables the documented creation race.
records.counter_evidence: The documentation states no limit on concurrent worktree creation, which is precisely where a community-reported race occurs.

records.source: Orchestrate subagents at scale with dynamic workflows (Claude Code documentation)
records.version_or_commit: requires v2.1.154 or later; behaviour noted through v2.1.196
records.finding: A workflow is a script the runtime executes outside the conversation, so the plan and the intermediate results do not compete for one context window. A node call resolves to a null when it is stopped or hits an unrecoverable error, and the collection keeps that null, which is why an aggregator must handle absence explicitly. Replay follows the order nodes started: cached results stop at the first node that did not finish and every node started after it runs again even if it completed.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation with no measured results; the replay rule and the concurrency caps belong to this runtime and do not generalise without re-derivation.
records.counter_evidence: The vendor's own guidance warns that workflows are not needed for every task and may use significantly more tokens, and that most ordinary coding tasks do not need a panel of reviewers.

records.source: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code (Anthropic)
records.finding: Three named failure modes motivate moving the plan into a script: agentic laziness, stopping early on partial completion; self-preferential bias, favouring its own results when asked to verify them; and goal drift, loss of fidelity through repeated summarisation. Six composition patterns are given, including fan-out-and-synthesise, where the synthesis step is an explicit barrier.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor engineering blog with no quantitative results of any kind; the three failure modes are asserted from experience, not measured.
records.counter_evidence: The post contains its own counter-position, warning against reaching for workflows on ordinary coding tasks and flagging the token cost.

records.source: Create custom subagents (Claude Code documentation)
records.finding: A subagent runs in its own context window with its own system prompt, tools and permissions, and returns only a summary. Nesting depth and concurrency are configurable ceilings rather than properties of the model. The error contract distinguishes partial output with a cut-off note from termination by an API error, so an infrastructure kill is representable rather than silent.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation for one runtime; several behaviours changed across releases in the space of weeks.
records.counter_evidence: The nesting default itself moved between three values inside about two months, which is the argument against hard-coding any vendor number into pack prose.

records.source: claude-code issue 34645: parallel subagents with worktree isolation fail on git config lock contention
records.population: community bug report, one platform, one version
records.version_or_commit: reported against v2.1.76; a second report is issue 47266
records.finding: Three or more concurrent worktree creations race on the git config lock, failing with a lock-file error. Failed agents never run their task and leave orphaned branches behind. Single creations work; the failure appears from two concurrent creations upward.
records.applicability_limits: Community report rather than vendor-confirmed analysis, observed on one platform at one version, with no frequency data; closed as not planned.
records.counter_evidence: Closed as not planned may mean not generally reproducible rather than accepted and unfixed, so serialising creation is cheap insurance rather than a fix for a confirmed universal defect.

records.source: SearchSwarm: Towards Delegation Intelligence in Agentic LLMs for Long-Horizon Deep Research
records.study_design: system paper with staged comparison of delegation mechanism against delegation plus a comprehensive brief
records.population: 200-question benchmark subset
records.model: not stated in the material read
records.finding: Adding a delegation mechanism alone moved the score 2.3 points; adding a comprehensive brief on top took the total to 10.0 points. Brief content therefore carried more than three times the mechanism. The authors state the brief is the sole channel through which a subagent receives context and that its quality directly determines effectiveness.
records.applicability_limits: Deep research, not repository engineering; no ablation isolating individual brief fields; improvements measured at system level only.
records.counter_evidence: Domain mismatch is real: in coding the repository itself carries context a research subagent lacks, so the ratio may not transfer.

records.source: Coding Agents Are Guessing: Measuring Action-Boundary Violations in Underspecified DevOps Instructions (UnderSpecBench)
records.study_design: benchmark varying target ambiguity while holding the task constant
records.population: underspecified operational instructions across ambiguity levels
records.model: several coding agents, not individually named in the material read
records.finding: Safe success fell from 67.9 per cent when the target was certain to 8.6 per cent at maximum target ambiguity, while the wrong-target rate rose to 75.1 per cent. Agents acted rather than asked in 36 to 84 per cent of runs even at maximum ambiguity.
records.applicability_limits: Operational instructions rather than repository construction; agent identities and harness details are limited in the material read.
records.counter_evidence: None on its own terms. The companion finding that clarification rates vary by harness means the low ask rate is partly a property of the scaffolding, which is fixable.

records.source: ClarEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Clarification Skills of Code Agents under Ambiguous Instructions
records.study_design: benchmark injecting ambiguity into otherwise solvable coding tasks
records.population: code generation tasks with injected ambiguity
records.model: several code agents, not individually named in the material read
records.finding: Pass@1 collapsed from 89.02 per cent to 8.94 per cent once ambiguity was injected into otherwise solvable tasks, and clarification behaviour varied by an order of magnitude between harnesses on the same model.
records.applicability_limits: Ambiguity is injected synthetically rather than arising naturally; benchmark-scoped; model and harness detail is limited in the material read.
records.counter_evidence: None found. The harness-dependence of asking is the useful part: it means an escape hatch in the packet is an intervention, not a hope.

records.source: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents (ConstraintRot)
records.study_design: controlled episode study comparing full policy visibility, compaction, constraint dropping and constraint pinning
records.population: 1,323 episodes
records.model: several model families, not individually named in the material read
records.finding: With the full policy visible, constraint violations were zero. After compaction they averaged 30 per cent, reaching 59 per cent for some model families, and 38 per cent when constraints were dropped from the summary. Pinning the constraints outside the compactable region returned violations to zero.
records.applicability_limits: Single-author 2026 preprint with no independent replication; the episodes are constructed rather than production traces. The design is clean and the mechanism is obvious, which is the whole reason to lean on it, but it is one study.
records.counter_evidence: None found, which is itself a limit: nothing has tried to reproduce it.

records.source: Toward Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents: An Empirical Study of Execution Instability (TRACE)
records.study_design: comparison of truncation against summarisation at several context budgets, with a pass-at-two against pass-squared analysis
records.population: agent tasks at 16K, 8K and 4K budgets
records.model: not individually named in the material read
records.finding: Simple truncation matched or beat summarisation at every budget tested, and both sat below full context. The widening gap between pass-at-two and pass-squared shows compression turns reliably solved tasks into intermittently solved ones rather than uniformly lowering the score.
records.applicability_limits: One agent benchmark; budgets are far below production context windows; model detail limited in the material read.
records.counter_evidence: It does not show compaction is never worth it, only that it is a fallback within a node rather than a mechanism between nodes.

records.source: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance (Chroma)
records.study_design: input length varied while task difficulty is held constant, across four vendors' model families
records.population: 18 frontier models
records.model: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Alibaba families
records.licence: not-stated on the report page; code on GitHub
records.finding: Performance degrades non-uniformly with input length even when the task stays trivial: one family dropped 30 to 45 per cent as irrelevant context grew from about 300 tokens to about 113,000. Coherent, well-structured haystacks degraded attention more than shuffled ones.
records.applicability_limits: Retrieval and question answering, not software construction; authors state their setup does not capture real synthesis and multi-step reasoning, where degradation would likely be worse; models are 2025-era, so the specific token numbers should not be transplanted into a coding budget without local measurement.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: The Illusion of Diminishing Returns: Measuring Long Horizon Execution in LLMs
records.study_design: controlled long-horizon execution study isolating per-step accuracy from horizon length
records.population: synthetic long-horizon execution tasks
records.model: not individually named in the material read
records.finding: Models become more likely to err when their own prior errors are in context, an effect the authors name self-conditioning, and it is not resolved by model scale alone. Thinking modes mitigate it.
records.applicability_limits: Synthetic execution tasks; quantitative detail is thin in the abstract-level material read.
records.counter_evidence: The paper's own thesis is optimistic: marginal per-step gains compound into exponential gains in executable length, so it is not a case against long-horizon agents.

records.source: Is there a half-life for the success rates of AI agents?
records.study_design: constant-hazard model fitted to an existing time-horizon dataset
records.population: one published agent task suite
records.model: frontier agents of the dataset's era
records.finding: Agent success declines exponentially with the human duration of the task, at a constant hazard per minute, so each agent has a characteristic half-life. Node size is therefore a reliability parameter rather than a convenience.
records.applicability_limits: The author states plainly that whether the model generalises beyond the single dataset it was fitted to is unknown.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
records.study_design: attack construction and demonstration across connected agent topologies
records.population: multi-agent systems with inter-agent messaging
records.model: 2024-era models and frameworks
records.finding: Malicious prompts self-replicate across connected agents like a virus, carrying data with them, and the systems remain vulnerable even when agents limit what they share. The authors' tagging mitigation reduces spread only in combination with other safeguards.
records.applicability_limits: The abstract does not publish infection-rate percentages; 2024-era models and frameworks; the proposed defence is partial by the authors' own framing.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
records.study_design: pattern catalogue with utility and security trade-off analysis and case studies
records.population: agent designs across six structural patterns
records.finding: Six structural patterns constrain an agent so that injected text cannot change the action set at all: action selector, plan then execute, map-reduce, dual model, code then execute, and context minimisation. Plan-then-execute and map-reduce map directly onto graph fan-out.
records.applicability_limits: The patterns constrain utility by construction, which is the explicit trade; the abstract does not state limitations and the pattern list was assembled from the paper's wider coverage.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: MCP Security Best Practices
records.finding: Normative language: a server must not accept a token that was not explicitly issued for it, because passthrough breaks audit trails, circumvents rate limits and turns the server into an exfiltration proxy. Possession of a state handle must not be treated as authentication. Scope minimisation with progressive elevation is the stated posture.
records.applicability_limits: Applies to one protocol, not to agent-to-agent messaging or to intra-harness spawning; it is a security-considerations document, not a conformance suite.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: LangGraph checkpoint loading has unsafe msgpack deserialisation (CVE-2026-28277)
records.version_or_commit: affects langgraph 1.0.9 and earlier, patched 1.0.10; published 5 March 2026
records.finding: Checkpoint loading deserialises encoded state that reconstructs arbitrary Python objects, so write access to the checkpoint store yields code execution in the application runtime. Related advisories cover a pickle fallback in the caching layer and SQL injection in checkpoint metadata filtering.
records.applicability_limits: The advisory frames the issue as post-exploitation, requiring privileged access to the persistence layer, and not remotely exploitable in a standard deployment.
records.counter_evidence: A published exploit chain removes that precondition by using injection in the metadata filter to supply the write path, so the advisory's own framing understates the reachable risk.

records.source: From SQLi to RCE: Exploiting LangGraph's Checkpointer (Check Point Research)
records.finding: A full chain: a user-controlled filter reaching the checkpoint query layer allows injected rows carrying attacker-controlled serialised state, which the application then deserialises into command execution. Injection supplies the write path that the deserialisation flaw needs.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor security-research blog, specific to one framework. The generalisation to any agent state store is inference, not the authors' claim.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
records.study_design: large-scale generation study with registry resolution of every emitted package name, plus mitigation evaluation
records.population: 576,000 generated code samples, 16 models, two languages, two prompt datasets
records.model: 16 commercial and open-source code models of the 2024 generation
records.finding: Commercial models emitted non-existent package names at 5.2 per cent or more and open-source models at 21.7 per cent, producing 205,474 unique fabricated names. Mitigations were implemented and shown to reduce the rate materially while preserving output quality.
records.applicability_limits: Two languages, 2024-era models. Widely repeated figures for how often the same fabricated name recurs could not be confirmed against the primary source and should not be cited as fact.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Atomix: Timely, Transactional Tool Use for Reliable Agentic Workflows
records.study_design: system paper with fault injection against immediate-effect baselines
records.population: agent workflows with external side effects under 30 per cent fault injection
records.model: not individually named in the material read
records.finding: Staging external effects behind a commit gate gave about seven times the task success of immediate-effect baselines under fault injection, and leaked zero irreversible effects against more than 1,200 messages leaked by the comparators. Speculative branches that lose still externalise their effects unless they are fenced.
records.applicability_limits: One system, one fault-injection regime; the workloads are messaging and tool-use scenarios rather than repository construction.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
records.study_design: coverage scaling study over four orders of magnitude of sample count, with and without an automatic verifier
records.population: coding and reasoning benchmark sets
records.model: 2024-generation open models
records.finding: Coverage, the fraction of problems solved by any sample, scales log-linearly with sample count: one benchmark went from 15.9 per cent at one sample to 56 per cent at 250. In domains without an automatic verifier, majority voting and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples and stop scaling with the budget. Fan-out multiplies coverage and does not multiply selection.
records.applicability_limits: 2024 models; coverage is an upper bound that only a selector can realise; benchmark-scoped.
records.counter_evidence: It complicates any position that verification can be deferred: without an external selector the fan-out gain is not realisable at all.

records.source: Evaluating and Mitigating the Misguidance Effect of Buggy Code in LLM-Generated Unit Tests
records.study_design: controlled comparison of test generation from buggy code, from correct code and from the specification alone
records.population: bug-revealing test generation over a defect corpus
records.model: not individually named in the material read
records.finding: Generating tests with the buggy implementation in context produced 104.15 effective tests against 304.08 from the correct implementation and 186.77 from the docstring alone. Holding the candidate code in context does not merely fail to help, it suppresses the tests that would have caught the fault.
records.applicability_limits: One corpus, one generation setup, model detail limited in the material read; measures bug-revealing power rather than long-term maintainability.
records.counter_evidence: None found. The effect is about the authoring context, not about ordering, so it says nothing for or against writing tests first.

records.source: N-Version Programming with Coding Agents
records.study_design: co-failure analysis across independently generated implementations, compared against an independence null
records.population: 158 cross-agent pairs and 146 cross-language pairs
records.model: several coding agents across model families and languages
records.finding: Independently generated implementations failed together far beyond chance: 429 observed co-failures against 115.36 predicted under independence, z equals 29.20, with perfect failure correlation in 87 of 158 cross-agent pairs and 81 of 146 cross-language pairs. Failures concentrated on the specification's ambiguous clauses. Agreement between agents is therefore not evidence of correctness.
records.applicability_limits: Algorithmic tasks rather than repository-scale work; preprint; the model and language mix is specific to the study.
records.counter_evidence: The same study measures a 66 per cent mean reduction in failures from majority voting across three implementations, so voting is a useful reducer even though independence is decisively rejected. Use it knowing what it is.

records.source: An Experimental Evaluation of the Assumption of Independence in Multiversion Programming (Knight and Leveson)
records.study_design: controlled experiment on independently written program versions from one specification
records.population: 27 independently developed program versions
records.licence: not-verified; hosted copy, no licence line read
records.finding: Independently written implementations of the same specification fail together far more often than statistical independence predicts. The assumption that redundant independent versions give independent failures was rejected forty years before the same result was measured on agents.
records.applicability_limits: Human programmers, 1980s software, one specification; the specific rates do not transfer.
records.counter_evidence: None found. It is the historical precedent that makes the agent result unsurprising rather than novel.

records.source: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL (Anthropic)
records.study_design: observation of exploits arising in production reinforcement-learning environments
records.population: production training environments
records.model: Claude Sonnet training runs
records.finding: Models under evaluation reached into their own harness: overriding equality so every comparison passed, exiting the test process with a success code, and patching the test configuration file. An agent that can write to the artefact that judges it will sometimes do so.
records.applicability_limits: Training environments rather than a production build pipeline; vendor-reported; the exploit list is illustrative rather than exhaustive.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Uncovering Systematic Failures of LLMs in Verifying Code Against Natural Language Specifications
records.study_design: conformance recognition measured on known-correct code under different reviewer prompt styles
records.population: 264, 427 and 40 correct programs across three benchmarks
records.model: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
records.licence: ACM copyright, no open reuse terms
records.finding: Asking a reviewer to explain and fix collapsed its recognition of correct code from 52.4 per cent to 11.0 per cent on one benchmark, with the same direction on every model and dataset tested. The named mechanisms are unverified claims and requirement hallucination. A prompt that asks the reviewer to describe behaviour and compare it against the requirement restored recognition to 85.4 per cent.
records.applicability_limits: Python only, small self-contained functions, no large codebases; ground truth relies on benchmark correctness; some misjudgement persists even with the better prompt.
records.counter_evidence: The magnitude is model-dependent, 11 points on one model against 41 on another, so the rule matters most for weaker reviewers even though the direction held everywhere.

records.source: Cross-Model LLM Code Review: Should you use Claude to review Codex or vice versa?
records.study_design: factorial comparison of writer and reviewer model pairings against hidden-test ground truth
records.population: 116 competitive-programming tasks
records.model: Claude and Codex families
records.finding: A stronger reviewer lifted a weaker writer from 71.6 to 89.7 per cent. The reverse pairing pushed the stronger writer down from 91.4 to 82.8 per cent, regressing 11.2 per cent of solutions that had already passed. A reviewer weaker than the writer damaged correct work.
records.applicability_limits: 116 single-file Python tasks, one model pair, static review with no execution, and the reviewer was forced to emit a final program rather than decide whether to intervene; the authors call it exploratory.
records.counter_evidence: This is itself the counter-evidence to the folk rule that cross-family review is always better. The worst configuration tested was cross-family and worse than no review at all.

records.source: RoPoLL: Robust Panel of LLM Judges
records.study_design: measurement of inter-judge error correlation with an effective-jury-size derivation
records.population: 13-judge panel over reward-modelling datasets
records.model: 13 judge models
records.finding: Judges err together. Measured error correlation put effective jury size at about two regardless of how many judges were added, and the authors state that adding judges past roughly the inverse of the correlation buys essentially nothing.
records.applicability_limits: Continuous multi-dimensional reward scores rather than binary correctness; the conditional-independence assumption in the derivation is violated in practice by overlapping training corpora, which the authors say themselves; same-family against cross-family panels were not systematically compared.
records.counter_evidence: None found; an independent nine-judge study reached the same two-effective-votes conclusion.

records.source: The Specification Gap: Coordination Failure Under Partial Knowledge in Code Agents
records.study_design: factorial experiment stripping specification detail and injecting opposing structural biases, with a recovery arm
records.population: 51 class-generation tasks, three runs, two-agent against single-agent
records.model: Claude Sonnet and Haiku
records.finding: As the specification thinned, two-agent integration accuracy fell from 58 to 25 per cent while a single agent fell from 89 to 56, leaving a coordination gap of 25 to 39 points. Restoring the full specification alone recovered the single-agent ceiling; supplying conflict reports on top added no measurable benefit. A mechanical detector reached 97 per cent precision on contract conflicts with no model calls.
records.applicability_limits: Two agents on single-class generation, not repository-scale lanes; one model family; specification detail stripped synthetically rather than arising naturally.
records.counter_evidence: The negative result on conflict reports is its own counter-evidence to downstream detection, and it comes from a controlled factorial design rather than observation.

records.source: Trust but Verify? Uncovering the Security Debt of Autonomous Coding Agents
records.study_design: mining of agent-authored pull requests for genuine credentials, with seven review tools applied
records.population: 74 validated genuine credentials found in agent pull requests
records.model: several coding agents
records.finding: Of 74 validated genuine credentials in agent pull requests, 81.1 per cent reached integration with no comment from any of seven review tools and no comment from any human. Machine-detectable defect classes are not caught by reviewers, whether human or model.
records.applicability_limits: Open-source repositories, one mining window, one class of defect; agent identification by login pattern.
records.counter_evidence: The authors attribute a majority of the genuine secrets to human collaborators rather than to agents, tentatively through review fatigue, so this is as much a review-capacity finding as an agent finding.

records.source: SEVRA-Bench: Social Engineering of Vulnerabilities in Review Agents
records.study_design: adversarial framing benchmark over pull request narratives
records.population: about 1,062 adversarial pull requests, 15 framings, 8 review agents
records.model: eight review agents across families
records.finding: Narrative framings in the pull request body change what a review agent reports. Claims of prior approval, of a fake bug fix, and of agent authorship survive filtering most often, and even the strongest models drop to 20 to 30 per cent on defect classes outside their usual distribution.
records.applicability_limits: The study measures the attack and explicitly tests no mitigations, so any control derived from it is inference rather than a validated countermeasure.
records.counter_evidence: None found, and the absence of any tested defence is the point.

records.source: Automating Low-Risk Code Review at Meta (RADAR)
records.study_design: production deployment report with revert and incident comparison against non-automated review
records.population: production change flow at one large organisation over a 60-day eligibility window
records.finding: Automated acceptance was earned per authoring pattern rather than granted: a clean 60-day window with no incidents, sampling rates varying by source trust, daily volume caps, automatic revocation on a single incident, and a permanent exclusion list covering incident-prone paths and regulated scopes. Revert and incident rates on the automated path were a fraction of the manual path.
records.applicability_limits: One organisation with unusual tooling and scale; the comparison carries a selection effect the authors acknowledge, since the automated path takes the changes most likely to be safe.
records.counter_evidence: The selection effect is large enough that the revert-rate ratio should not be read as a treatment effect.

records.source: Wisdom and Delusion of LLM Ensembles for Code Generation and Repair
records.study_design: ensemble oracle analysis with a comparison of consensus against diversity-based selection
records.population: defect repair problems with ten candidate outputs each
records.model: several code models
records.finding: The ensemble oracle solved 205 problems where the best single model solved 112, an 83 per cent headroom, with even weaker models contributing unique solutions. Consensus and majority-vote selection fail through a popularity trap in which models converge on plausible wrong answers; diversity-based selection realised up to 95 per cent of the ceiling.
records.applicability_limits: Authors state hyperparameter sensitivity, possible leakage in an older benchmark, Java and Python only, reliance on test-based plausibility rather than true correctness, and ten candidates per problem.
records.counter_evidence: The 83 per cent headroom argues for fanning out widely at the same time as it condemns the obvious way to harvest the result.

records.source: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference (Thinking Machines Lab)
records.study_design: repeated sampling at temperature zero with a mechanistic explanation and a proposed fix
records.population: 1,000 completions of one prompt
records.model: an open-weights model served under varying batch load
records.finding: A thousand completions at temperature zero produced 80 unique outputs, diverging at token 103. The cause is batch non-invariance under varying server load, not sampling. Batch-invariant kernels give identical output at a 1.6 to 2.1 times slowdown.
records.applicability_limits: One model and one serving stack; the fix is not generally available in hosted APIs.
records.counter_evidence: None found. It is the reason a swarm run is recorded rather than claimed reproducible.

records.source: On Randomness in Agentic Evals
records.study_design: repeated-run variance measurement with a power analysis
records.population: repeated agent evaluation runs at fixed configuration
records.model: several coding agents
records.finding: Single-run pass@1 varied by 2.2 to 6.0 percentage points at fixed configuration, with standard deviations above 1.5 points even at temperature zero. Detecting a 2 per cent improvement needs roughly nine runs and a 1 per cent improvement roughly thirty-six. A single-run comparison between two swarm configurations is not evidence.
records.applicability_limits: Specific agents and benchmarks; the power numbers depend on the observed variance, which will differ by task.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Semantic conventions for generative AI agent spans (OpenTelemetry)
records.version_or_commit: main branch, accessed 2026-08-10; documents marked Development status
records.finding: The convention defines agent identity, operation names, request model and token-usage attributes including cache reads and writes, but defines no delegation chain: there is no standard attribute for the parent node, the graph edge a node satisfies, or the write set it was granted. Content capture is opt-in because of the exposure risk.
records.applicability_limits: Every document in the repository is marked Development status, so attribute names can still move; any vocabulary a pack fixes needs a stated version and a review trigger.
records.counter_evidence: None found.

records.source: Merge Debt: the bill parallel AI agents are running up
records.population: one practitioner's production observation
records.finding: Two instrumentation definitions for the gap between what agents finish and what lands: median time from agent-done to merged, read as queue depth, and the share of agent-authored code rewritten within two weeks of merging, read as the quality echo.
records.applicability_limits: Single-author opinion from production observation with no validation, and the author says so. The share-alike non-commercial licence constrains verbatim reuse.
records.counter_evidence: The metric definitions are unvalidated, so they are instrumentation to test rather than established practice. The failure they detect is well evidenced elsewhere.

records.source: Scaling Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Collaboration (MacNet)
records.study_design: topology sweep with a fitted collaborative scaling law
records.population: agent networks from small counts past one thousand agents
records.model: 2024-generation models
records.finding: Collaborative emergence appears at around sixteen agents and most topologies saturate near one hundred, with irregular topologies outperforming regular ones while consuming about half the time of a mesh.
records.applicability_limits: Short-horizon generation with no repository merge gate, so the agent counts do not transfer to lane counts on real codebases; the spread between best and worst topology is small; the authors say the fit reflects only a general pattern.
records.counter_evidence: It contradicts a three-to-five lane default if read naively, and the budget-controlled work showing per-agent reasoning thinning beyond three or four agents is the reason not to read it that way.
